/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 09 June 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2818 (-98)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4441 (-278)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2205 (-13)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1614 (18)
Baltic Handysize Index: 868 (3)
CAPESIZE
A softer session for the market, with both basins coming under pressure as limited activity and thin enquiry weighed on rates. The BCI 5TC fell sharply, down $2,524 on the day to settle at $40,274. In the Pacific, sentiment was clearly softer from the outset, with very little activity to provide support. The absence of miner demand remained the key factor, with only a single C5 miner active during the day. This lack of participation translated directly into thinner volumes and increased downward pressure on rates. C5 dropped by $0.955 to $12.180, with fixtures reportedly done at $12.25 early on before slipping into the low $12s as the day progressed. The Atlantic basin also eased, with a similarly subdued tone throughout. In the south, the Brazil market is becoming increasingly date sensitive, with early July cargoes seeing limited bids. Offers for 1/10 July laycan were heard in the low to mid $36s, while forward positions were reportedly fixed at discounted levels, reinforcing the softer outlook. Activity out of West Africa to China remained muted, and in the North Atlantic, sentiment continued to weaken amid a lack of fresh enquiry. On C3, rates declined by $0.605 to $35.650.
PANAMAX
The Atlantic market is said to be showing a slightly more improved tone, with brokers noting a relatively busier feel, particularly as tonnage from the North Continent is reportedly seeing increased demand. However, despite this marginal uptick in activity the tonnage list remains relatively long. Market participants have also highlighted that fronthaul from North Coast South America is appearing comparatively more active, suggesting a modest shift in demand dynamics within the basin. The Pacific market is reportedly continuing on a downward trajectory with some divergence in pricing emerging between cargo types with mineral stems commanding a slight premium over grain cargoes. Meanwhile, the shorter Indonesian trades remain under pressure as an increasing supply of tonnage continues to weigh on the market, prompting owners to revise offers downward amid weakening sentiment. Period fixtures have been reported today along with the CL Dalian (81,578 2014) open in Qinzhou 9 June fixing for two laden legs but further details lacked. The P5TC displayed a shift downwards of $120 to $19,846.

Asia
The Predator (81,754 2019) open Cailan 9 June is said to have been placed on subjects for an East Coast Australia round, while the Aomari (82,009 2014) open Hon Gai 12 June was also said to have fixed a similar run. The Alpha Legacy (82,047 2018) open Zhoushan 10/11 June has been reported as on subjects for a North Pacific trip around the low to mid $20,000s. Meanwhile, the Ordu (81,660 2012) open Qinghuangdao 8/9 June was said to be on subjects, but no other details emerged, and the Ocean Pride (82,399 2021) open Penglai 13 June has been said to have fixed for a short round.
SUPRAMAX
Continuing from yesterday there was a rather optimistic tone to the market today. Brokers said that stronger numbers were again being discussed n the Atlantic from the US Gulf certainly for trans Atlantic runs, although little fresh fixing surfaced. It was heard that the Belmar (63,641 2021) open Puerto Quetzal was fixed for a fronthaul at $23,000 recently, but no more details came to light. Again, from South Atlantic some felt that there appeared to be a little more enquiry, helping owners’ interest. From Asia, brokers said that backhaul enquiry had entered into play from the north which was helped to under pin demand from both the NoPac and Australia, again actual fixtures remained under the radar. The 11TC average closed the day up $228 at $20,396.
HANDYSIZE
The sector enjoyed a more positive day, with a firmer tone prevailing, particularly in Asian markets. The BHSI added 3 points to close at 868, while the 7TC average rose $64 to finish at $15,629. In the Continent–Mediterranean region, sentiment was fairly balanced, with rates on the firmer side as the tonnage list shortened. The South Atlantic and US Gulf continued to display steady activity, with available tonnage and cargo demand well balanced. In the Pacific, market views were slightly mixed, some sources noted steady activity, while others felt the rate rise was primarily due to increased demand and tighter tonnage, though overall the market remained firm.

Atlantic
A 38,000 was heard fixed for a trip from Canakkale to US East Coast with cement at $12,000 plus $160,000 in lieu of hold cleaning by Bainbridge, with no further details revealed.

Asia
The Lefkada (37,951 2016) open Fangcheng 16 June fixed for a trip from Cailan to Tahara with wood pellet in the high teens by Swire, again lacking further details.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Iron Ore and Steel Trade Slows in May

Based on preliminary customs figures from China, iron ore imports dipped 0.4 Mt year-on-year, reaching a three-month low of 97.7 Mt in May. Umetal reports that after a downward trend throughout May, iron ore inventories at 42 tracked port locations grew 1.2 Mt to 164.0 Mt in the week to 5 June.

Steel trade activity also moderated in May, with exports decreasing 0.2 Mt to 10.3 Mt, bringing Jan-May shipments 6.7 Mt lower to 41.7 Mt, preliminary customs data show. Meanwhile, May steel imports held steady at approximately 0.5 Mt, bringing the year-to-May total 0.3 Mt lower to 2.3 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
An active day Cape FFA, trading over 8,000 lots for the day, with the majority of the action focused on the Jul, Q3 and Q4 contracts. Jun traded $36750 down to $36250, and closing at the lows of the day. Jul traded down to $30000 in the morning before an afternoon of better bids and paid up to $31000, closing at $30650 for the day. Q3 traded $30600 up to $31250, closing at $31050. Q4 traded 30750 up to $31650, closing off the highs at $31450. C27 featured a few times, printing only $26,400. C28 traded between $22850-$22900.

PMX
PMX paper came off in the morning then recovered in the afternoon printing relatively flat across the curve. Jun was active from the open, trading down to 20,500 early before recovering and spending much of the afternoon around 20,800. Jul saw the most volume cleared, initially trading at a low of 20,700 before pushing higher through the day, printing up to 21,350 and finishing around 21,15

A SOFTER PACIFIC TONE IS ALSO BEGINNING TO FEATURE IN DISCUSSIONS, WITH EXPECTATIONS OF INCREASED BALLASTER INFLOW INTO ECSA POTENTIALLY WEIGHING ON FORWARD SENTIMENT. OUTLOOK: THE ATLANTIC MARKET HAS SO FAR PROVEN RELATIVELY RESILIENT DESPITE A MORE CAUTIOUS BACKDROP. HOWEVER, LIMITED FIXING VOLUME AND WIDE BID/OFFER SPREADS SUGGEST THE MARKET IS STILL SEARCHING FOR DIRECTION. FOR NOW, THE MOST LIKELY NEAR-TERM OUTCOME APPEARS TO BE A CONTINUATION OF THE CURRENT SIDEWAYS TREND, UNLESS A MORE MEANINGFUL PICK-UP IN FRESH DEMAND EMERGES. PAC SHORT: THE WEEK OPENED ON A FAIRLY NEGATIVE NOTE WITH THE SPOT TONNAGE, MAINLY IN THE SOUTH, STRUGGLING TO FIND HOMES AND CONTINUING TO DROP OFFERS FOR BOTH EAUS AND INDO. NOPAC LIQUIDITY IS PARTICULARLY THIN WITH FIXTURES BEING COMPLETED AROUND $19.5K BKI CJK ON MONDAY. GENERIC OFFERS FOR NOPAC GRAINS HAVE BEEN AROUND $21K BKI FOR TONNAGE OPENING NEXT WEEK, BUT BIDS ARE SCARCE. THE EAUS CARGO LIST IS STILL LACKING WITH A LARGE PROPORTION OF THE CHINESE MARKET AT COALTRANS BEIJING. MONDAY FIXING SAW EAUS/SCHINA FIXING AT 21K BKI WHICH WAS REPEATED ON TUESDAY FOR MORE ECO UNITS. HOWEVER, THERE IS LITTLE SIGN OF THIS BEING A FLOOR WITH MULTIPLE EAUS OFFERS CIRCA 21.5K BKI CJK. OWNERS SEEMINGLY AREN'T SEEING A PLETHORA OF OPTIONS AND ARE THEREFORE HAVING TO COUNTER AGAINST THEMSELVES UNTIL “CHEAP” OFFERS ARE GETTING TRACTION. THE FLOW INTO INDIA HAS BEEN VERY THIN FOR BOTH EAUS AND INDO AMIDST AMPLE DOMESTIC COAL SUPPLY. BHP STEMS ARE BEING SOLD AROUND 21K BKI CJK FOR 1H JULY DATES WITH OPERATORS LOOKING TO TAKE FORWARD COVER AS THERE IS LITTLE SIGN OF A LARGE INFLUX OF FRESH CARGO TO BALANCE OUT THE CONTINUALLY LENGTHENING TONNAGE LIST. THERE WERE WHISPERS OF THE INDO MARKET FINDING A FLOOR AT THE END OF LAST WEEK BUT WITHOUT STRONG BUYING PRESENCE FROM THE CHINESE WE HAVE SEEN LOWS OF MID 17’S-18K BKI HK BEING DONE FOR INDO/SCHINA MID JUNE DATES. HOWEVER, RISING CONGESTION IN S.CHINA IS PUSHING A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER OF VESSELS' OPEN DATES BACK, EASING SOME PRESSURE FROM TONNAGE AVAILABILITY ON THE PROMPT SIDE. OVERALL, THERE IS LITTLE FUNDAMENTAL SIGNS OF THE MARKET TURNING IN OWNERS FAVOUR SO FAR SO WE EXPECT THE MARKET TO CONTINUE TO FALL UNTIL THE TONNAGE LIST IS CLEARED OUT AND THE CARGO COUNT REGAINS SOME DEPTH. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场分化明显，好望角型船市场大幅走弱（BDI跌98点至2818，BCI急挫278点），大西洋和太平洋需求均承压；巴拿马型船稳中趋弱，跨大西洋航线有所改善但太平洋持续下滑；超灵便型和灵便型船逆势上扬，显示区域细分市场分化。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: BDI指数下跌98点至2818，好望角型船领跌（BCI-278至4441），太平洋煤炭铁矿石航线需求疲软；巴拿马型船持平略降（-13点），大西洋航线因欧洲需求略显韧性；超灵便型和灵便型船指数小幅上扬，反映出小型船市场相对抗跌。FFA曲线显示近期合约大幅贴水，Capesize Jun26 $36,250，Panamax Jun26 $20,775。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: 好望角型船：C5太平洋航线$12.18创新低，澳矿商压价明显，巴西-中国C3航线$35.65趋弱；巴拿马型船：P1A大西洋$17,200反弹，P3A太平洋$20,875下跌，印尼/澳洲煤炭航线供给压力加大；超灵便型：S3西非航线$21,850跳涨$500，S4A美湾-北欧$29,718涨幅$575；灵便型：南美东海岸航线HS3 $20,522稳中走强。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注好望角型船太平洋市场何时企稳，澳矿商低价吸货后若需求回暖可布局反弹；巴拿马型船关注北大陆-远东航线P2A $27,209的支撑位表现；超灵便型美湾-北欧S4A航线继续强势，季内交易机会可期；FFA市场近月贴水深，Q3/Q4价差收窄提供跨月套利空间。

跨大西洋往返航线升至$17,200（+55），欧洲大陆需求回暖支撑价格，但期租市场bid/offer价差仍宽，市场方向未明，短期偏震荡。
